- C1C2C3CC1C23: This represents a complex cage-like structure (likely a norbornane or similar derivative)
- C=O: A carbonyl group

Without visualization, I'll need to carefully count the hydrogen environments. In 1H NMR, hydrogens in the same chemical environment produce the same signal.

The molecule appears to be a bridged polycyclic structure with:
- A hydroxyl group (OH): This hydrogen will give one peak
- Hydrogens attached to the carbon skeleton: These will give peaks based on their unique environments
- No hydrogens on the carbonyl carbon

Based on the SMILES notation, this appears to be a highly constrained cage structure. In such structures, many of the hydrogens can be in unique environments due to the rigid 3D structure.

From my analysis of similar cage structures, this molecule likely has 5 distinct hydrogen environments:
1. The hydroxyl hydrogen (OH)
2-5. Four distinct types of C-H hydrogens in the cage structure due to their different positions relative to the OH and C=O groups
